options.A: Ground-level ozone is a harmful air pollutant and component of photochemical smog; stratospheric ozone protects life from ultraviolet radiation
options.B: Ground-level ozone protects life; stratospheric ozone is harmful

questions.explanation: Ground-level ozone is a harmful air pollutant and component of photochemical smog; stratospheric ozone protects life from ultraviolet radiation.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about El Niño and the Indian monsoon is correct?

options.A: El Niño can influence the Indian monsoon but does not determine rainfall in every year
options.B: El Niño determines rainfall in every year

questions.explanation: El Niño can influence the Indian monsoon but does not determine rainfall in every year.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Paris Agreement and Kyoto Protocol is correct?

options.A: The Paris Agreement is under the UNFCCC; the Kyoto Protocol is an earlier climate treaty
options.B: The Kyoto Protocol is under the UNFCCC; the Paris Agreement is an earlier climate treaty
options.C: Both are under the Montreal Protocol

questions.explanation: The Paris Agreement is under the UNFCCC; the Kyoto Protocol is an earlier climate treaty.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Montreal Protocol and Kigali Amendment is correct?

options.A: The Montreal Protocol concerns ozone-depleting substances; the Kigali Amendment phases down HFCs, which generally do not deplete ozone but are potent greenhouse gases
options.B: The Montreal Protocol concerns greenhouse gases; the Kigali Amendment phases down ozone-depleting substances

questions.explanation: The Montreal Protocol concerns ozone-depleting substances; the Kigali Amendment phases down HFCs; HFCs generally do not deplete ozone but are potent greenhouse gases.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, Water Act 1974 and Air Act 1981 is correct?

options.A: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 is an umbrella law; Water Act 1974 and Air Act 1981 address specific pollution areas
options.B: The Water Act 1974 is an umbrella law
options.C: The Air Act 1981 is an umbrella law

questions.explanation: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 is an umbrella law; Water Act 1974 and Air Act 1981 address specific pollution areas.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 is correct?

options.A: It was renamed in 2023 as the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980; older exam sources may retain the old title
options.B: It was renamed in 2023 as the Forest Protection Act, 2023
options.C: It was renamed in 2023 as the Forest Management Act, 2023
options.D: It was renamed in 2023 as the Forest Conservation Act, 2023

questions.explanation: The Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 was renamed in 2023 as the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980; older exam sources may retain the old title.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Article 48A and Article 51A(g) is correct?

options.A: Article 48A is a Directive Principle for the State; Article 51A(g) is a Fundamental Duty of citizens
options.B: Article 48A is a Fundamental Duty; Article 51A(g) is a Directive Principle

questions.explanation: Article 48A is a Directive Principle for the State; Article 51A(g) is a Fundamental Duty of citizens.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the launch years of Project Tiger, Project Elephant and Swachh Bharat Mission is correct?

options.A: Project Tiger began in 1973; Project Elephant began in 1992; Swachh Bharat Mission began on 2 October 2014
options.B: Project Tiger began in 1992; Project Elephant began in 1973; Swachh Bharat Mission began on 2 October 2014
options.C: Project Tiger began in 1973; Project Elephant began in 2014; Swachh Bharat Mission began in 1992
options.D: Project Tiger began in 2014; Project Elephant began in 1992; Swachh Bharat Mission began in 1973

questions.explanation: Project Tiger began in 1973; Project Elephant began in 1992; Swachh Bharat Mission began on 2 October 2014.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about energy flow and nutrient cycling is correct?

options.A: Energy flows through an ecosystem and is not recycled; nutrients such as carbon and nitrogen cycle through ecosystems
options.B: Energy is recycled and nutrients flow one-way
options.C: Both energy and nutrients are recycled
options.D: Both energy and nutrients flow one-way

questions.explanation: Energy flows through an ecosystem and is not recycled; nutrients such as carbon and nitrogen cycle through ecosystems.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about pyramids of numbers and biomass is correct?

options.A: Pyramids of numbers and biomass may be inverted; the pyramid of energy is always upright
options.B: All pyramids are always upright
options.D: Only the pyramid of energy may be inverted

questions.explanation: The pyramid of energy is always upright. Pyramids of numbers and biomass may be inverted.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about habitat and niche is correct?

options.A: Habitat means the place an organism lives; niche means its ecological role and resource-use pattern
options.B: Habitat means the ecological role; niche means the place an organism lives
options.C: Habitat and niche are the same
options.D: Habitat is for animals; niche is for plants

questions.explanation: Habitat means the place an organism lives; niche means its ecological role and resource-use pattern.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about afforestation and reforestation is correct?

options.A: Afforestation establishes forest on land not recently forested; reforestation restores forest on previously forested land
options.B: Afforestation restores forest on previously forested land; reforestation establishes forest on land not recently forested
options.D: Afforestation is for timber; reforestation is for wildlife

questions.explanation: Afforestation establishes forest on land not recently forested; reforestation restores forest on previously forested land.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about IUCN threatened categories is correct?

options.A: IUCN threatened categories are CR, EN and VU; Near Threatened and Data Deficient are not threatened categories
options.B: IUCN threatened categories are NT and DD
options.C: IUCN threatened categories are LC and NT
options.D: IUCN threatened categories are EX and EW

questions.explanation: IUCN threatened categories are CR, EN and VU. Near Threatened and Data Deficient are not threatened categories.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about India's biodiversity hotspots is correct?

options.A: India lies within four biodiversity hotspots: Himalaya, Indo-Burma, Western Ghats-Sri Lanka and Sundaland
options.B: India lies within two biodiversity hotspots
options.C: India lies within three biodiversity hotspots
options.D: India lies within five biodiversity hotspots

questions.explanation: India lies within four biodiversity hotspots: Himalaya, Indo-Burma, Western Ghats-Sri Lanka and Sundaland.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about PM2.5 and PM10 is correct?

options.A: PM2.5 is finer than PM10 and can penetrate deeper into the respiratory tract
options.B: PM10 is finer than PM2.5 and can penetrate deeper into the respiratory tract

questions.explanation: PM2.5 is finer than PM10 and can penetrate deeper into the respiratory tract.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about high BOD is correct?

options.A: High BOD indicates a substantial biodegradable organic load in many water-quality contexts
options.B: High BOD indicates low organic pollution
options.C: High BOD indicates high oxygen levels

questions.explanation: High BOD indicates a substantial biodegradable organic load in many water-quality contexts.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Kyoto Protocol and Paris Agreement is correct?

options.A: The Paris Agreement is under the UNFCCC; the Kyoto Protocol is an earlier climate treaty
options.B: The Kyoto Protocol is under the UNFCCC; the Paris Agreement is an earlier climate treaty
options.C: Both are under the Montreal Protocol

questions.explanation: The Paris Agreement is under the UNFCCC; the Kyoto Protocol is an earlier climate treaty.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Montreal Protocol and Kigali Amendment is correct?

options.A: The Montreal Protocol concerns ozone-depleting substances; the Kigali Amendment phases down HFCs, which generally do not deplete ozone but are potent greenhouse gases
options.B: The Montreal Protocol concerns greenhouse gases; the Kigali Amendment phases down ozone-depleting substances

questions.explanation: The Montreal Protocol concerns ozone-depleting substances; the Kigali Amendment phases down HFCs; HFCs generally do not deplete ozone but are potent greenhouse gases.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, Water Act 1974 and Air Act 1981 is correct?

options.A: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 is an umbrella law; Water Act 1974 and Air Act 1981 address specific pollution areas
options.B: The Water Act 1974 is an umbrella law
options.C: The Air Act 1981 is an umbrella law

questions.explanation: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 is an umbrella law; Water Act 1974 and Air Act 1981 address specific pollution areas.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 is correct?

options.A: It was renamed in 2023 as the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980; older exam sources may retain the old title
options.B: It was renamed in 2023 as the Forest Protection Act, 2023
options.C: It was renamed in 2023 as the Forest Management Act, 2023
options.D: It was renamed in 2023 as the Forest Conservation Act, 2023

questions.explanation: The Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 was renamed in 2023 as the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980; older exam sources may retain the old title.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Article 48A and Article 51A(g) is correct?

options.A: Article 48A is a Directive Principle for the State; Article 51A(g) is a Fundamental Duty of citizens
options.B: Article 48A is a Fundamental Duty; Article 51A(g) is a Directive Principle

questions.explanation: Article 48A is a Directive Principle for the State; Article 51A(g) is a Fundamental Duty of citizens.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the launch years of Project Tiger, Project Elephant and Swachh Bharat Mission is correct?

options.A: Project Tiger began in 1973; Project Elephant began in 1992; Swachh Bharat Mission began on 2 October 2014
options.B: Project Tiger began in 1992; Project Elephant began in 1973; Swachh Bharat Mission began on 2 October 2014
options.C: Project Tiger began in 1973; Project Elephant began in 2014; Swachh Bharat Mission began in 1992
options.D: Project Tiger began in 2014; Project Elephant began in 1992; Swachh Bharat Mission began in 1973

questions.explanation: Project Tiger began in 1973; Project Elephant began in 1992; Swachh Bharat Mission began on 2 October 2014.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the term 'ecology' is correct?

options.A: The term was introduced by Ernst Haeckel in 1866
options.B: The term was introduced by Charles Darwin in 1859
options.C: The term was introduced by Raymond Lindeman in 1942
options.D: The term was introduced by Aristotle in 350 BC

questions.explanation: Ernst Haeckel, a German biologist, introduced the term 'Okologie' in 1866.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the scope of ecology is correct?

options.A: It includes organisms, populations, communities, ecosystems, biomes, the biosphere, energy flow, nutrient cycling, biodiversity and human impacts on nature
options.B: It includes only organisms and populations
options.C: It includes only ecosystems and biomes
options.D: It includes only human impacts on nature

questions.explanation: Ecology's scope includes organisms, populations, communities, ecosystems, biomes, the biosphere, energy flow, nutrient cycling, biodiversity and human impacts on nature.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the two broad components of an ecosystem is correct?

options.A: Biotic components (living organisms) and abiotic components (non-living physical and chemical factors)
options.B: Producers and consumers only

questions.explanation: The two broad components of an ecosystem are biotic components (living organisms) and abiotic components (non-living physical and chemical factors).

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is an abiotic component of an ecosystem?

options.A: Temperature
options.B: Green plants

questions.explanation: Abiotic components include non-living factors such as sunlight, temperature, water, air, soil, minerals, pH, salinity and humidity.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is a biotic component of an ecosystem?

options.A: Green plants
options.B: Sunlight

questions.explanation: Biotic components are living components, commonly grouped as producers, consumers and decomposers; green plants are an example.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a producer?

options.A: Green plants
options.B: Deer

questions.explanation: Producers are autotrophs that manufacture organic food from inorganic substances, usually through photosynthesis; green plants, algae and some bacteria are examples.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a primary consumer?

options.A: Deer
options.B: Tiger

questions.explanation: Primary consumers feed directly on producers; they are commonly herbivores such as deer, rabbits and grasshoppers.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a secondary consumer?

options.A: Frog
options.B: Deer

questions.explanation: Secondary consumers feed on primary consumers; they may be carnivores or omnivores; frog is an example.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a tertiary consumer?

options.A: Eagle
options.B: Deer

questions.explanation: Tertiary consumers feed on secondary consumers and often occupy higher trophic positions in a food chain; eagle is an example.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a decomposer?

options.A: Bacteria
options.B: Deer

questions.explanation: Decomposers, especially bacteria and fungi, break down dead organic matter and wastes into simpler substances, returning nutrients to the environment.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a detritivore?

options.A: Earthworm
options.B: Deer

questions.explanation: A detritivore ingests dead organic matter or detritus, such as earthworms and many millipedes; detritivores differ from microbial decomposers.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a grazing food chain?

options.A: Grass → grasshopper → frog → snake → eagle
options.B: Dead leaves → earthworm → bird

questions.explanation: Grass → grasshopper → frog → snake → eagle is a grazing food chain; the exact chain varies by ecosystem.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about a food web is correct?

options.A: A food web is a network of interconnected food chains that represents the multiple feeding relationships in an ecosystem
options.B: A food web is a single linear sequence of energy transfer
options.C: A food web is a pyramid of numbers
options.D: A food web is a group of decomposers

questions.explanation: A food web is a network of interconnected food chains that represents the multiple feeding relationships in an ecosystem.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about trophic levels is correct?

options.A: Producers are generally the first trophic level, herbivores the second and successive consumers higher levels
options.B: Producers are the highest trophic level
options.C: Herbivores are the first trophic level
options.D: Carnivores are the first trophic level

questions.explanation: A trophic level is the feeding position an organism occupies in a food chain; producers are generally the first trophic level, herbivores the second and successive consumers higher levels.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the 10 percent law of energy transfer is correct?

options.A: Raymond Lindeman's ecological generalisation states that, on average, only about 10% of energy at one trophic level is transferred to the next; the actual proportion varies
options.B: It states that 100% of energy is transferred to the next trophic level
options.C: It states that 50% of energy is transferred to the next trophic level
options.D: It states that energy is recycled at each trophic level

questions.explanation: Raymond Lindeman's ecological generalisation states that, on average, only about 10% of energy at one trophic level is transferred to the next; the actual proportion varies.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about energy flow in an ecosystem is correct?

options.A: Energy flows in one direction through trophic levels—from sunlight or chemical energy to producers and consumers—and is ultimately dissipated as heat; it is not recycled
options.B: Energy is recycled in a cyclic manner
options.C: Energy flows from consumers back to producers
options.D: Energy flows randomly in all directions

questions.explanation: Energy flows in one direction through trophic levels—from sunlight or chemical energy to producers and consumers—and is ultimately dissipated as heat; it is not recycled.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about ecological pyramids is correct?

options.A: An ecological pyramid is a graphical representation of the number, biomass or energy of organisms at successive trophic levels
options.B: An ecological pyramid is a network of food chains
options.C: An ecological pyramid is a linear sequence of energy transfer
options.D: An ecological pyramid is a group of decomposers

questions.explanation: An ecological pyramid is a graphical representation of the number, biomass or energy of organisms at successive trophic levels.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the three types of ecological pyramids is correct?

options.A: The three types are pyramid of numbers, pyramid of biomass and pyramid of energy
options.B: The three types are pyramid of producers, consumers and decomposers
options.C: The three types are pyramid of herbivores, carnivores and omnivores
options.D: The three types are pyramid of air, water and soil

questions.explanation: The three types of ecological pyramids are pyramid of numbers, pyramid of biomass and pyramid of energy.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the pyramid of energy is correct?

options.A: The pyramid of energy is always upright because usable energy decreases at each successive trophic transfer
options.B: The pyramid of energy is always inverted
options.C: The pyramid of energy can be upright or inverted
options.D: The pyramid of energy is always irregular

questions.explanation: The pyramid of energy is always upright because usable energy decreases at each successive trophic transfer.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the pyramid of numbers is correct?

options.A: The pyramid of numbers can be inverted; for example, one tree may support many insects and parasites
options.B: The pyramid of numbers is always upright
options.C: The pyramid of numbers is always inverted
options.D: The pyramid of numbers is always irregular

questions.explanation: Yes. For example, one tree may support many insects and parasites, producing an inverted or irregular pyramid of numbers.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the pyramid of biomass is correct?

options.A: The pyramid of biomass can be inverted; in some aquatic ecosystems, the standing biomass of phytoplankton is lower than that of zooplankton at a given moment
options.B: The pyramid of biomass is always upright
options.C: The pyramid of biomass is always inverted
options.D: The pyramid of biomass is always irregular

questions.explanation: Yes. In some aquatic ecosystems, the standing biomass of phytoplankton is lower than that of zooplankton at a given moment because phytoplankton reproduce and turn over rapidly.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about ecological balance is correct?

options.A: Ecological balance is a dynamic condition in which interactions and natural processes maintain ecosystem functions and populations within changing limits; it does not mean that nature is static
options.B: Ecological balance is a static condition where nothing changes
options.C: Ecological balance means populations never change
options.D: Ecological balance means only producers exist

questions.explanation: Ecological balance is a dynamic condition in which interactions and natural processes maintain ecosystem functions and populations within changing limits; it does not mean that nature is static.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about ecological succession is correct?

options.A: Ecological succession is the gradual change in species composition and community structure in an area over time, often following the formation of new habitat or disturbance
options.B: Ecological succession is a sudden change in species composition
options.C: Ecological succession is the migration of animals
options.D: Ecological succession is the formation of a food web

questions.explanation: Ecological succession is the gradual change in species composition and community structure in an area over time, often following the formation of new habitat or disturbance.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about primary succession is correct?

options.A: Primary succession begins on a surface without developed soil, such as newly exposed rock or fresh lava
options.B: Primary succession occurs after a fire where soil remains
options.C: Primary succession occurs in abandoned farmland
options.D: Primary succession occurs in a mature forest

questions.explanation: Primary succession begins on a surface without developed soil, such as newly exposed rock or fresh lava.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about secondary succession is correct?

options.A: Secondary succession occurs where a community has been disturbed but soil or biological legacies remain, such as after a fire or abandoned cultivation
options.B: Secondary succession begins on bare rock
options.C: Secondary succession occurs on fresh lava
options.D: Secondary succession occurs in a newly formed pond

questions.explanation: Secondary succession occurs where a community has been disturbed but soil or biological legacies remain, such as after a fire or abandoned cultivation.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about pioneer species is correct?

options.A: A pioneer species first colonises a newly formed or disturbed habitat and helps modify conditions for later communities; lichens and mosses can be pioneers on bare rock
options.B: A pioneer species is the last species to arrive in a community
options.C: A pioneer species only lives in climax communities
options.D: A pioneer species never changes its habitat

questions.explanation: A pioneer species first colonises a newly formed or disturbed habitat and helps modify conditions for later communities; lichens and mosses can be pioneers on bare rock.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about climax communities is correct?

options.A: A climax community is a traditional term for a relatively stable late-successional community under a given set of conditions; modern ecology recognises that communities may remain dynamic and need not reach one fixed climax
options.B: A climax community is the first community to colonise bare rock
options.D: A climax community consists only of pioneer species

questions.explanation: A climax community is a traditional term for a relatively stable late-successional community under a given set of conditions; modern ecology recognises that communities may remain dynamic and need not reach one fixed climax.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about a habitat is correct?

options.A: A habitat is the natural place or environment in which an organism lives and obtains the conditions and resources it needs
options.B: A habitat is the functional role of a species in an ecosystem
options.C: A habitat is the feeding position of an organism
options.D: A habitat is a group of individuals of the same species

questions.explanation: A habitat is the natural place or environment in which an organism lives and obtains the conditions and resources it needs.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about an ecological niche is correct?

options.A: An ecological niche is the functional role of a species in an ecosystem, including its resource use, environmental requirements, interactions and position in the food web
options.B: An ecological niche is the physical location where an organism lives
options.C: An ecological niche is the number of individuals in a population
options.D: An ecological niche is the total biomass of an ecosystem

questions.explanation: An ecological niche is the functional role of a species in an ecosystem, including its resource use, environmental requirements, interactions and position in the food web.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the difference between habitat and niche is correct?

options.A: Habitat describes where an organism lives; niche describes how it lives and functions, including what it uses and how it interacts
options.B: Habitat describes how an organism lives; niche describes where it lives
options.C: Habitat and niche are the same thing
options.D: Habitat is for animals; niche is for plants

questions.explanation: Habitat describes where an organism lives; niche describes how it lives and functions, including what it uses and how it interacts.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about population ecology is correct?

options.A: Population ecology is the study of population size, density, distribution, age structure, growth, birth rates, death rates and migration
options.B: Population ecology is the study of communities only
options.C: Population ecology is the study of ecosystems only
options.D: Population ecology is the study of biomes only

questions.explanation: Population ecology is the study of population size, density, distribution, age structure, growth, birth rates, death rates and migration.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about a population is correct?

options.A: A population is a group of individuals of the same species living in a particular area at a particular time and potentially interbreeding
options.B: A population is all species living in an area
options.C: A population is a group of different species interacting
options.D: A population is the non-living components of an area

questions.explanation: A population is a group of individuals of the same species living in a particular area at a particular time and potentially interbreeding.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about population density is correct?

options.A: Population density is the number of individuals of a population per unit area or volume
options.B: Population density is the total number of species in an area
options.C: Population density is the total biomass of an ecosystem
options.D: Population density is the number of trophic levels in a food chain

questions.explanation: Population density is the number of individuals of a population per unit area or volume.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about a community in ecology is correct?

options.A: A community in ecology is all populations of different species living and interacting in a particular area
options.B: A community in ecology is a group of individuals of the same species
options.C: A community in ecology is the non-living components of an area
options.D: A community in ecology is a single food chain

questions.explanation: A community in ecology is all populations of different species living and interacting in a particular area.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about community ecology is correct?

options.A: Community ecology is the study of species composition, diversity, interactions, food webs and changes within ecological communities
options.B: Community ecology is the study of population size only
options.C: Community ecology is the study of individual organisms only
options.D: Community ecology is the study of abiotic factors only

questions.explanation: Community ecology is the study of species composition, diversity, interactions, food webs and changes within ecological communities.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about carrying capacity is correct?

options.A: Carrying capacity is the maximum population size an environment can sustain over time under prevailing resource and environmental conditions; it can change when conditions change
options.B: Carrying capacity is the minimum population size for survival
options.C: Carrying capacity is the total number of species in an area
options.D: Carrying capacity is the rate of energy transfer between trophic levels

questions.explanation: Carrying capacity is the maximum population size an environment can sustain over time under prevailing resource and environmental conditions; it can change when conditions change.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about mutualism is correct?

options.A: Mutualism is an interaction in which both species benefit; examples include pollinating insects receiving nectar while pollinating flowers
options.B: Mutualism is an interaction where one species benefits and the other is harmed
options.C: Mutualism is an interaction where one species benefits and the other is unaffected
options.D: Mutualism is an interaction where both species are harmed

questions.explanation: Mutualism is an interaction in which both species benefit; examples include pollinating insects receiving nectar while pollinating flowers.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about commensalism is correct?

options.A: Commensalism is an interaction in which one species benefits and the other is neither significantly helped nor harmed; examples often cited include epiphytic orchids growing on trees
options.B: Commensalism is an interaction where both species benefit
options.C: Commensalism is an interaction where both species are harmed
options.D: Commensalism is an interaction where one species is harmed and the other is unaffected

questions.explanation: Commensalism is an interaction in which one species benefits and the other is neither significantly helped nor harmed; examples often cited include epiphytic orchids growing on trees.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about parasitism is correct?

options.A: Parasitism is an interaction in which a parasite benefits while the host is harmed; examples include tapeworms in humans and ticks on mammals
options.B: Parasitism is an interaction where both species benefit
options.C: Parasitism is an interaction where one species benefits and the other is unaffected
options.D: Parasitism is an interaction where both species are harmed

questions.explanation: Parasitism is an interaction in which a parasite benefits while the host is harmed; examples include tapeworms in humans and ticks on mammals.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about predation is correct?

options.A: Predation is an interaction in which one organism (predator) captures and consumes another (prey)
options.B: Predation is an interaction where both species benefit
options.C: Predation is an interaction where one species is unaffected
options.D: Predation is an interaction where both species are harmed

questions.explanation: Predation is an interaction in which one organism (predator) captures and consumes another (prey).

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about competition in ecology is correct?

options.A: Competition is an interaction in which organisms use the same limited resource, reducing access or success for one or both competitors
options.B: Competition is an interaction where both species benefit
options.C: Competition is an interaction where one species is unaffected
options.D: Competition is an interaction where one species benefits and the other is harmed

questions.explanation: Competition is an interaction in which organisms use the same limited resource, reducing access or success for one or both competitors.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about symbiosis is correct?

options.A: Symbiosis is a close, often long-term association between organisms of different species; it can include mutualism, commensalism or parasitism depending on the effects
options.B: Symbiosis is an interaction where both species are harmed
options.C: Symbiosis is a type of competition
options.D: Symbiosis is a type of predation

questions.explanation: Symbiosis is a close, often long-term association between organisms of different species; it can include mutualism, commensalism or parasitism depending on the effects.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about amensalism is correct?

options.A: Amensalism is an interaction in which one species is harmed while the other is not significantly affected; antibiotic release by some microbes is a commonly cited example
options.B: Amensalism is an interaction where both species benefit
options.C: Amensalism is an interaction where one species benefits and the other is harmed
options.D: Amensalism is an interaction where both species are harmed

questions.explanation: Amensalism is an interaction in which one species is harmed while the other is not significantly affected; antibiotic release by some microbes is a commonly cited example.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about a biome is correct?

options.A: A biome is a large ecological region characterised by climate and dominant vegetation or other major biological features, such as tropical rainforest, desert, grassland and tundra
options.B: A biome is a small habitat within an ecosystem
options.C: A biome is a group of individuals of the same species
options.D: A biome is the non-living components of an area

questions.explanation: A biome is a large ecological region characterised by climate and dominant vegetation or other major biological features, such as tropical rainforest, desert, grassland and tundra.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the biosphere is correct?

options.A: The biosphere is the global zone of life on Earth, comprising parts of the atmosphere, hydrosphere and lithosphere where organisms occur
options.B: The biosphere is only the atmosphere
options.C: The biosphere is only the hydrosphere
options.D: The biosphere is only the lithosphere

questions.explanation: The biosphere is the global zone of life on Earth, comprising parts of the atmosphere, hydrosphere and lithosphere where organisms occur.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about a natural resource is correct?

options.A: A natural resource is a material, organism or environmental feature occurring in nature that people or ecosystems use, such as water, soil, forests, minerals, sunlight and wind
options.B: A natural resource is only minerals found underground
options.C: A natural resource is only water resources
options.D: A natural resource is only forest resources

questions.explanation: A natural resource is a material, organism or environmental feature occurring in nature that people or ecosystems use, such as water, soil, forests, minerals, sunlight and wind.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about renewable resources is correct?

options.A: Renewable resources are replenished naturally on a human timescale when managed sustainably, such as solar, wind and sustainably harvested biological resources
options.B: Renewable resources form much more slowly than they are consumed
options.D: Renewable resources cannot be used by humans

questions.explanation: Renewable resources are replenished naturally on a human timescale when managed sustainably, such as solar, wind and sustainably harvested biological resources.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about non-renewable resources is correct?

options.A: Non-renewable resources form much more slowly than they are consumed, such as coal, petroleum, natural gas and many mineral deposits
options.B: Non-renewable resources are replenished quickly
options.D: Non-renewable resources are only used for food

questions.explanation: Non-renewable resources form much more slowly than they are consumed, such as coal, petroleum, natural gas and many mineral deposits.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about forest resources is correct?

options.A: Forest resources are goods and ecosystem services supplied by forests, including timber, fuelwood, food, medicines, habitat, carbon storage, soil protection and water regulation
options.B: Forest resources are only timber and fuelwood
options.C: Forest resources are only medicinal plants
options.D: Forest resources are only wildlife habitat

questions.explanation: Forest resources are goods and ecosystem services supplied by forests, including timber, fuelwood, food, medicines, habitat, carbon storage, soil protection and water regulation.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the importance of forests is correct?

options.A: Forests support biodiversity, store carbon, regulate local and regional water cycles, protect soil, reduce erosion and provide livelihoods and resources
options.B: Forests only provide timber

questions.explanation: Forests support biodiversity, store carbon, regulate local and regional water cycles, protect soil, reduce erosion and provide livelihoods and resources.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about water resources is correct?

options.A: Water resources include surface water, groundwater, rainwater, glaciers and other freshwater sources used by people and ecosystems
options.B: Water resources are only surface water

questions.explanation: Water resources include surface water, groundwater, rainwater, glaciers and other freshwater sources used by people and ecosystems.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about groundwater is correct?

options.A: Groundwater is water stored below Earth's surface in saturated soil and rock formations, including aquifers
options.B: Groundwater is water in rivers and lakes
options.C: Groundwater is water in the atmosphere

questions.explanation: Groundwater is water stored below Earth's surface in saturated soil and rock formations, including aquifers.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about an aquifer is correct?

options.A: An aquifer is a permeable geological formation that can store and transmit usable quantities of groundwater
options.B: An aquifer is a type of soil
options.C: An aquifer is a surface water body
options.D: An aquifer is a type of forest

questions.explanation: An aquifer is a permeable geological formation that can store and transmit usable quantities of groundwater.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about soil resources is correct?

options.A: Soil provides a medium for plant growth, stores and filters water, cycles nutrients, supports organisms and underpins agriculture and terrestrial ecosystems
options.B: Soil is only a source of minerals
options.C: Soil is only a medium for construction

questions.explanation: Soil provides a medium for plant growth, stores and filters water, cycles nutrients, supports organisms and underpins agriculture and terrestrial ecosystems.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about mineral resources is correct?

options.A: Mineral resources are naturally occurring inorganic substances or deposits that can be extracted for metals, industrial minerals and construction materials
options.B: Mineral resources are only metals
options.C: Mineral resources are only fossil fuels
options.D: Mineral resources are only renewable resources

questions.explanation: Mineral resources are naturally occurring inorganic substances or deposits that can be extracted for metals, industrial minerals and construction materials.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about energy resources is correct?

options.A: Energy resources are sources used to produce useful energy, including fossil fuels, nuclear fuels and renewable sources such as solar, wind, hydro, biomass and geothermal energy
options.B: Energy resources are only fossil fuels
options.C: Energy resources are only solar and wind energy
options.D: Energy resources are only nuclear fuels

questions.explanation: Energy resources are sources used to produce useful energy, including fossil fuels, nuclear fuels and renewable sources such as solar, wind, hydro, biomass and geothermal energy.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about conservation of natural resources is correct?

options.A: Conservation of natural resources is protection, restoration and careful use of natural resources to maintain their availability, ecological functions and benefits for present and future generations
options.B: Conservation is only protecting forests

questions.explanation: Conservation of natural resources is protection, restoration and careful use of natural resources to maintain their availability, ecological functions and benefits for present and future generations.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about sustainable utilisation is correct?

options.A: Sustainable utilisation is using resources at rates and in ways that maintain ecological integrity and do not undermine the ability of future generations to meet their needs
options.B: Sustainable utilisation is using resources as fast as possible
options.C: Sustainable utilisation is not using any resources at all
options.D: Sustainable utilisation is using only renewable resources

questions.explanation: Sustainable utilisation is using resources at rates and in ways that maintain ecological integrity and do not undermine the ability of future generations to meet their needs.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about deforestation is correct?

options.A: Deforestation is large-scale removal or conversion of forest cover to another land use, such as agriculture, settlement, mining or infrastructure
options.B: Deforestation is planting trees in a new area

questions.explanation: Deforestation is large-scale removal or conversion of forest cover to another land use, such as agriculture, settlement, mining or infrastructure.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the major causes of deforestation is correct?

options.A: Major causes of deforestation include agricultural expansion, commercial logging, fuelwood collection, mining, roads, urbanisation, dams, fires and other land-use changes
options.B: The only cause of deforestation is agricultural expansion
options.C: The only cause of deforestation is commercial logging
options.D: The only cause of deforestation is urbanisation

questions.explanation: Major causes of deforestation include agricultural expansion, commercial logging, fuelwood collection, mining, roads, urbanisation, dams, fires and other land-use changes.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the major effects of deforestation is correct?

options.A: Major effects of deforestation include habitat loss, biodiversity decline, soil erosion, disrupted water cycles, increased carbon emissions, local climate changes and impacts on forest-dependent communities
options.B: The only effect of deforestation is habitat loss
options.C: The only effect of deforestation is increased carbon emissions
options.D: The only effect of deforestation is soil erosion

questions.explanation: Major effects of deforestation include habitat loss, biodiversity decline, soil erosion, disrupted water cycles, increased carbon emissions, local climate changes and impacts on forest-dependent communities.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about afforestation is correct?

options.A: Afforestation is the establishment of forest on land that has not recently been forested, according to the definition used by the relevant programme or inventory
options.B: Afforestation is the re-establishment of forest on land that was previously forested but has been cleared or degraded
options.C: Afforestation is the removal of forest cover
options.D: Afforestation is the protection of existing forests

questions.explanation: Afforestation is the establishment of forest on land that has not recently been forested, according to the definition used by the relevant programme or inventory.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about reforestation is correct?

options.A: Reforestation is the re-establishment of forest on land that was previously forested but has been cleared or degraded
options.B: Reforestation is the establishment of forest on land that has not recently been forested
options.C: Reforestation is the removal of forest cover
options.D: Reforestation is the protection of existing forests

questions.explanation: Reforestation is the re-establishment of forest on land that was previously forested but has been cleared or degraded.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the difference between afforestation and reforestation is correct?

options.A: Afforestation creates forest on land not recently forested; reforestation restores forest on previously forested land
options.B: Afforestation restores forest on previously forested land; reforestation creates forest on land not recently forested
options.D: Afforestation is for timber; reforestation is for wildlife

questions.explanation: Afforestation creates forest on land not recently forested; reforestation restores forest on previously forested land.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about soil erosion is correct?

options.A: Soil erosion is the detachment and movement of topsoil by water, wind, ice or human activity
options.B: Soil erosion is the formation of new soil
options.C: Soil erosion is the compaction of soil
options.D: Soil erosion is the pollution of soil

questions.explanation: Soil erosion is the detachment and movement of topsoil by water, wind, ice or human activity.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the major causes of soil erosion is correct?

options.A: Major causes of soil erosion include removal of vegetation, overgrazing, deforestation, inappropriate cultivation, construction, mining, intense rainfall and wind
options.B: The only cause of soil erosion is deforestation
options.C: The only cause of soil erosion is overgrazing
options.D: The only cause of soil erosion is intense rainfall

questions.explanation: Major causes of soil erosion include removal of vegetation, overgrazing, deforestation, inappropriate cultivation, construction, mining, intense rainfall and wind.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about controlling soil erosion is correct?

options.A: Soil erosion can be controlled by maintaining vegetation cover, practising contour ploughing and terracing, using cover crops and mulching, building check dams, managing grazing and protecting riparian zones
options.B: Soil erosion can be controlled by removing all vegetation
options.C: Soil erosion can be controlled by increasing overgrazing
options.D: Soil erosion can be controlled by removing check dams

questions.explanation: Soil erosion can be controlled by maintaining vegetation cover, practising contour ploughing and terracing, using cover crops and mulching, building check dams, managing grazing and protecting riparian zones.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about watershed management is correct?

options.A: Watershed management is integrated management of land, water and vegetation within a drainage area to conserve soil and water, reduce runoff and improve livelihoods and ecosystem health
options.B: Watershed management is management of a single river only
options.C: Watershed management is management of groundwater only
options.D: Watershed management is management of forests only

questions.explanation: Watershed management is integrated management of land, water and vegetation within a drainage area to conserve soil and water, reduce runoff and improve livelihoods and ecosystem health.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about a watershed is correct?

options.A: A watershed is an area of land from which all surface runoff drains to a common outlet, such as a stream, lake or river
options.B: A watershed is a type of aquifer
options.C: A watershed is a forest reserve
options.D: A watershed is a type of soil

questions.explanation: A watershed is an area of land from which all surface runoff drains to a common outlet, such as a stream, lake or river.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about rainwater harvesting is correct?

options.A: Rainwater harvesting is the collection and storage of rainwater from rooftops or land surfaces for later use or to recharge groundwater
options.B: Rainwater harvesting is the collection of river water
options.C: Rainwater harvesting is the collection of groundwater
options.D: Rainwater harvesting is the collection of seawater

questions.explanation: Rainwater harvesting is the collection and storage of rainwater from rooftops or land surfaces for later use or to recharge groundwater.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about common rainwater-harvesting methods is correct?

options.A: Common rainwater-harvesting methods include rooftop collection into tanks, recharge pits, recharge wells, percolation tanks, check dams, farm ponds and contour bunds
options.B: The only rainwater-harvesting method is rooftop collection
options.C: The only rainwater-harvesting method is check dams
options.D: The only rainwater-harvesting method is recharge wells

questions.explanation: Common rainwater-harvesting methods include rooftop collection into tanks, recharge pits, recharge wells, percolation tanks, check dams, farm ponds and contour bunds.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about groundwater conservation is correct?

options.A: Groundwater conservation helps maintain drinking-water supplies, irrigation, river baselines and ecosystem functions and reduces the risk of falling water tables and land subsidence
options.B: Groundwater conservation only helps in agriculture
options.C: Groundwater conservation only helps in industry

questions.explanation: Groundwater conservation helps maintain drinking-water supplies, irrigation, river baselines and ecosystem functions and reduces the risk of falling water tables and land subsidence.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about how groundwater can be conserved is correct?

options.A: Groundwater can be conserved by recharging aquifers, protecting wetlands and recharge zones, reducing leakage, using water-efficient irrigation, regulating extraction and reusing treated wastewater where safe
options.B: Groundwater can be conserved by increasing extraction
options.C: Groundwater can be conserved by draining wetlands
options.D: Groundwater can be conserved by increasing leakage

questions.explanation: Groundwater can be conserved by recharging aquifers, protecting wetlands and recharge zones, reducing leakage, using water-efficient irrigation, regulating extraction and reusing treated wastewater where safe.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about sustainable forest management is correct?

options.A: Sustainable forest management maintains forest biodiversity, productivity, regeneration, ecological processes and social benefits over time
options.B: Sustainable forest management maximises timber extraction
options.C: Sustainable forest management eliminates all human use
options.D: Sustainable forest management converts forests to agriculture

questions.explanation: Sustainable forest management maintains forest biodiversity, productivity, regeneration, ecological processes and social benefits over time.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the 3R principle in resource conservation is correct?

options.A: The 3R principle is Reduce consumption and waste, Reuse products and materials, and Recycle materials into useful products; reduction is generally preferred before recycling
options.B: The 3R principle is Remove, Replace and Restore
options.C: The 3R principle is Reduce, Remove and Rebuild
options.D: The 3R principle is Reuse, Restore and Recycle

questions.explanation: The 3R principle is Reduce consumption and waste, Reuse products and materials, and Recycle materials into useful products; reduction is generally preferred before recycling.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about biodiversity is correct?

options.A: Biodiversity is the variety and variability of life, including diversity within species, between species and among ecosystems
options.B: Biodiversity is only the number of species in an area

questions.explanation: Biodiversity is the variety and variability of life, including diversity within species, between species and among ecosystems.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the three main levels of biodiversity is correct?

options.A: The three main levels of biodiversity are genetic diversity, species diversity and ecosystem diversity
options.B: The three main levels are plant diversity, animal diversity and microbial diversity
options.C: The three main levels are terrestrial, aquatic and marine diversity
options.D: The three main levels are local, regional and global diversity

questions.explanation: The three main levels of biodiversity are genetic diversity, species diversity and ecosystem diversity.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about genetic diversity is correct?

options.A: Genetic diversity is variation in genes and alleles within a species or population, helping populations adapt to changing conditions
options.B: Genetic diversity is the variety of species in an area
options.C: Genetic diversity is the variety of ecosystems
options.D: Genetic diversity is the number of trophic levels

questions.explanation: Genetic diversity is variation in genes and alleles within a species or population, helping populations adapt to changing conditions.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about species diversity is correct?

options.A: Species diversity is the variety of species in an area and their relative abundance; it includes species richness and evenness
options.B: Species diversity is only the number of species in an area
options.C: Species diversity is only genetic variation
options.D: Species diversity is only ecosystem variety

questions.explanation: Species diversity is the variety of species in an area and their relative abundance; it includes species richness and evenness.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about ecosystem diversity is correct?

options.A: Ecosystem diversity is the variety of habitats, ecological communities and ecosystem processes across a region
options.B: Ecosystem diversity is the variety of genes within a species
options.C: Ecosystem diversity is the number of species in an area
options.D: Ecosystem diversity is the number of trophic levels

questions.explanation: Ecosystem diversity is the variety of habitats, ecological communities and ecosystem processes across a region.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about why biodiversity is important is correct?

options.A: Biodiversity supports ecosystem functioning and resilience and provides food, medicines, pollination, soil formation, water purification, climate regulation, cultural values and livelihoods
options.B: Biodiversity only provides food

questions.explanation: Biodiversity supports ecosystem functioning and resilience and provides food, medicines, pollination, soil formation, water purification, climate regulation, cultural values and livelihoods.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about a biodiversity hotspot is correct?

options.A: A biodiversity hotspot is a biogeographic region with exceptional plant endemism and severe habitat loss; the Conservation International criteria require at least 1,500 endemic vascular plant species and loss of at least 70% of original natural vegetation
options.B: A biodiversity hotspot is any area with many species
options.C: A biodiversity hotspot is a protected area only
options.D: A biodiversity hotspot is a region with no endemic species

questions.explanation: A biodiversity hotspot is a biogeographic region with exceptional plant endemism and severe habitat loss; the Conservation International criteria require at least 1,500 endemic vascular plant species and loss of at least 70% of original natural vegetation.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the number of global biodiversity hotspots is correct?

options.A: 36 biodiversity hotspots are commonly recognised in the current Conservation International framework
options.B: 25 biodiversity hotspots are commonly recognised

questions.explanation: 36 biodiversity hotspots are commonly recognised in the current Conservation International framework.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the biodiversity hotspots that include parts of India is correct?

options.A: India lies within four biodiversity hotspots: the Himalaya, Indo-Burma, Western Ghats-Sri Lanka and Sundaland; the Nicobar Islands are part of Sundaland
options.B: India lies within only one biodiversity hotspot
options.C: India lies within two biodiversity hotspots
options.D: India lies within three biodiversity hotspots

questions.explanation: India lies within four biodiversity hotspots: the Himalaya, Indo-Burma, Western Ghats-Sri Lanka and Sundaland; the Nicobar Islands are part of Sundaland.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about an endemic species is correct?

options.A: An endemic species is naturally restricted to a particular geographic area and found nowhere else in the wild
options.B: An endemic species is found everywhere in the world

questions.explanation: An endemic species is naturally restricted to a particular geographic area and found nowhere else in the wild.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about an endangered species is correct?

options.A: An endangered species faces a very high risk of extinction in the wild, corresponding to the IUCN Red List category Endangered (EN)
options.B: An endangered species faces no risk of extinction
options.C: An endangered species is found everywhere

questions.explanation: An endangered species faces a very high risk of extinction in the wild, corresponding to the IUCN Red List category Endangered (EN).

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about a vulnerable species is correct?

options.A: A vulnerable species faces a high risk of extinction in the wild, corresponding to the IUCN category Vulnerable (VU)
options.B: A vulnerable species faces a very high risk of extinction
options.C: A vulnerable species faces no risk of extinction
options.D: A vulnerable species is already extinct

questions.explanation: A vulnerable species faces a high risk of extinction in the wild, corresponding to the IUCN category Vulnerable (VU).

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about an extinct species is correct?

options.A: An extinct species is one for which there is no reasonable doubt that the last individual has died, corresponding to IUCN category Extinct (EX)
options.B: An extinct species faces a high risk of extinction
options.C: An extinct species is found in zoos only

questions.explanation: An extinct species is one for which there is no reasonable doubt that the last individual has died, corresponding to IUCN category Extinct (EX).

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about IUCN threatened species is correct?

options.A: Threatened species under the IUCN system are classified as Vulnerable (VU), Endangered (EN) or Critically Endangered (CR)
options.B: Threatened species are classified as Least Concern or Near Threatened
options.C: Threatened species are classified as Data Deficient only
options.D: Threatened species are classified as Extinct only

questions.explanation: Threatened species under the IUCN system are classified as Vulnerable (VU), Endangered (EN) or Critically Endangered (CR).

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the IUCN Red List is correct?

options.A: The IUCN Red List is the International Union for Conservation of Nature's global assessment system that evaluates extinction risk of species using defined criteria
options.B: The IUCN Red List is a list of protected areas in India
options.C: The IUCN Red List is a list of invasive species only
options.D: The IUCN Red List is a list of medicinal plants only

questions.explanation: The IUCN Red List is the International Union for Conservation of Nature's global assessment system that evaluates extinction risk of species using defined criteria.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the main IUCN Red List categories is correct?

options.A: The main IUCN Red List categories are Not Evaluated (NE), Data Deficient (DD), Least Concern (LC), Near Threatened (NT), Vulnerable (VU), Endangered (EN), Critically Endangered (CR), Extinct in the Wild (EW) and Extinct (EX)
options.B: The main categories are only Vulnerable, Endangered and Critically Endangered
options.C: The main categories are only Least Concern and Near Threatened
options.D: The main categories are only Extinct and Extinct in the Wild

questions.explanation: The main IUCN Red List categories are Not Evaluated (NE), Data Deficient (DD), Least Concern (LC), Near Threatened (NT), Vulnerable (VU), Endangered (EN), Critically Endangered (CR), Extinct in the Wild (EW) and Extinct (EX).

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Data Deficient species is correct?

options.A: Data Deficient means available information is insufficient to assess extinction risk; it does not mean low risk
options.B: Data Deficient means the species is safe
options.C: Data Deficient means the species is extinct
options.D: Data Deficient means the species is invasive

questions.explanation: No. Data Deficient means available information is insufficient to assess extinction risk; it does not mean low risk.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about wildlife conservation is correct?

options.A: Wildlife conservation is the protection and management of wild species and their habitats to maintain viable populations, ecological roles and genetic diversity
options.B: Wildlife conservation is only protecting tigers
options.C: Wildlife conservation is only protecting forests
options.D: Wildlife conservation is only protecting birds

questions.explanation: Wildlife conservation is the protection and management of wild species and their habitats to maintain viable populations, ecological roles and genetic diversity.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about ex-situ conservation is correct?

options.A: Ex-situ conservation is conservation outside natural habitats, such as in zoos, botanical gardens, seed banks, gene banks, tissue culture collections and captive-breeding programmes
options.B: Ex-situ conservation is the conservation of species in their natural habitats
options.C: Ex-situ conservation is conservation in national parks only
options.D: Ex-situ conservation is conservation in wildlife sanctuaries only

questions.explanation: Ex-situ conservation is conservation outside natural habitats, such as in zoos, botanical gardens, seed banks, gene banks, tissue culture collections and captive-breeding programmes.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about a national park in India is correct?

options.A: A national park in India is a protected area notified under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, with stronger restrictions on activities than many other protected-area categories; exact legal provisions and permitted rights are governed by the Act
options.B: A national park is a protected area under the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980
options.C: A national park is a protected area under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986
options.D: A national park is a protected area under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002

questions.explanation: A national park in India is a protected area notified under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, with stronger restrictions on activities than many other protected-area categories; exact legal provisions and permitted rights are governed by the Act.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about a wildlife sanctuary in India is correct?

options.A: A wildlife sanctuary in India is a protected area declared under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, for protecting wildlife and habitat, subject to the Act's restrictions and applicable rights/permissions
options.B: A wildlife sanctuary is a protected area under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986
options.C: A wildlife sanctuary is a protected area under the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980
options.D: A wildlife sanctuary is a protected area under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002

questions.explanation: A wildlife sanctuary in India is a protected area declared under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, for protecting wildlife and habitat, subject to the Act's restrictions and applicable rights/permissions.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about a biosphere reserve is correct?

options.A: A biosphere reserve is a large landscape designated under UNESCO's Man and the Biosphere Programme to promote biodiversity conservation alongside sustainable development and research; it commonly has core, buffer and transition zones
options.B: A biosphere reserve is a protected area under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972
options.C: A biosphere reserve is a protected area under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986
options.D: A biosphere reserve is a protected area under the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980

questions.explanation: A biosphere reserve is a large landscape designated under UNESCO's Man and the Biosphere Programme to promote biodiversity conservation alongside sustainable development and research; it commonly has core, buffer and transition zones.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the three zones of a biosphere reserve is correct?

options.A: The three zones of a biosphere reserve are core zone for strict conservation, buffer zone for compatible activities such as research and education, and transition zone where sustainable human activities occur
options.B: The three zones are inner zone, middle zone and outer zone
options.C: The three zones are protected zone, use zone and restoration zone
options.D: The three zones are forest zone, water zone and soil zone

questions.explanation: The three zones of a biosphere reserve are core zone for strict conservation, buffer zone for compatible activities such as research and education, and transition zone where sustainable human activities occur.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about a botanical garden is correct?

options.A: A botanical garden is a managed collection of living plants maintained for research, education, conservation and public display
options.B: A botanical garden is a facility that keeps wild animals
options.C: A botanical garden is a seed bank only
options.D: A botanical garden is a national park

questions.explanation: A botanical garden is a managed collection of living plants maintained for research, education, conservation and public display.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about a zoological park is correct?

options.A: A zoological park is a facility that keeps wild animals in managed conditions for conservation, education, research and, in some cases, breeding
options.B: A zoological park is a managed collection of living plants
options.C: A zoological park is a seed bank
options.D: A zoological park is a national park

questions.explanation: A zoological park is a facility that keeps wild animals in managed conditions for conservation, education, research and, in some cases, breeding.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about a wildlife corridor is correct?

options.A: A wildlife corridor is a strip or network of habitat connecting separated habitat patches and allowing movement of organisms, gene flow and access to resources
options.B: A wildlife corridor is a protected area under the Wildlife (Protection) Act
options.C: A wildlife corridor is a type of national park
options.D: A wildlife corridor is a type of biosphere reserve

questions.explanation: A wildlife corridor is a strip or network of habitat connecting separated habitat patches and allowing movement of organisms, gene flow and access to resources.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about human-wildlife conflict is correct?

options.A: Human-wildlife conflict refers to negative interactions between people and wild animals, such as crop damage, livestock predation, property damage, injury or loss of human life
options.B: Human-wildlife conflict is a type of conservation strategy
options.C: Human-wildlife conflict is a type of protected area
options.D: Human-wildlife conflict is a type of biodiversity hotspot

questions.explanation: Human-wildlife conflict refers to negative interactions between people and wild animals, such as crop damage, livestock predation, property damage, injury or loss of human life.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about how human-wildlife conflict can be reduced is correct?

options.A: Human-wildlife conflict can be reduced by protecting and restoring habitats and corridors, using locally appropriate barriers and early-warning systems, securing crops and livestock, managing waste and providing fair, timely compensation and community participation
options.B: Human-wildlife conflict can be reduced by eliminating all wildlife
options.C: Human-wildlife conflict can be reduced by eliminating all human activity
options.D: Human-wildlife conflict can be reduced by converting forests to agriculture

questions.explanation: Human-wildlife conflict can be reduced by protecting and restoring habitats and corridors, using locally appropriate barriers and early-warning systems, securing crops and livestock, managing waste and providing fair, timely compensation and community participation.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about an invasive alien species is correct?

options.A: An invasive alien species is a non-native species whose introduction or spread causes, or is likely to cause, environmental, economic or human-health harm
options.B: An invasive alien species is a native species that is common
options.C: An invasive alien species is an endangered species
options.D: An invasive alien species is an endemic species

questions.explanation: An invasive alien species is a non-native species whose introduction or spread causes, or is likely to cause, environmental, economic or human-health harm.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the difference between an alien species and an invasive species is correct?

options.A: An alien species occurs outside its natural range due to human activity or other introduction; it is termed invasive when it spreads and causes or is likely to cause harm
options.B: Alien and invasive are the same thing
options.C: An alien species is always harmful
options.D: An invasive species is always native

questions.explanation: An alien species occurs outside its natural range due to human activity or other introduction; it is termed invasive when it spreads and causes or is likely to cause harm.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about examples of invasive alien plants found in India is correct?

options.A: Examples include Lantana camara, Parthenium hysterophorus (Congress grass), Prosopis juliflora and water hyacinth (Pontederia crassipes, formerly Eichhornia crassipes); impacts vary by habitat
options.B: The only invasive alien plant in India is Lantana camara
options.C: The only invasive alien plant in India is water hyacinth
