options.D: The only invasive alien plant in India is Parthenium hysterophorus

questions.explanation: Examples include Lantana camara, Parthenium hysterophorus (Congress grass), Prosopis juliflora and water hyacinth (Pontederia crassipes, formerly Eichhornia crassipes); impacts vary by habitat.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the importance of biodiversity conservation in India is correct?

options.A: India contains diverse ecosystems and high species richness and endemism; conservation supports ecological services, livelihoods, cultural values and resilience to environmental change
options.B: India has no endemic species
options.D: Biodiversity has no role in India

questions.explanation: India contains diverse ecosystems and high species richness and endemism; conservation supports ecological services, livelihoods, cultural values and resilience to environmental change.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about India's major biodiversity-rich regions is correct?

options.A: Examples of India's major biodiversity-rich regions include the Himalaya, Western Ghats, north-eastern India, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, forests of central India, deserts, wetlands, coasts and marine ecosystems
options.B: India's only biodiversity-rich region is the Western Ghats
options.C: India's only biodiversity-rich region is the Himalaya
options.D: India's only biodiversity-rich region is the Andaman and Nicobar Islands

questions.explanation: Examples of India's major biodiversity-rich regions include the Himalaya, Western Ghats, north-eastern India, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, forests of central India, deserts, wetlands, coasts and marine ecosystems.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the importance of the Western Ghats for biodiversity is correct?

options.A: The Western Ghats are an ancient mountain chain with high rainfall gradients, varied habitats, high endemism and globally important freshwater and forest ecosystems
options.B: The Western Ghats are the largest desert in India
options.C: The Western Ghats have no endemic species
options.D: The Western Ghats are the youngest mountain range

questions.explanation: The Western Ghats are an ancient mountain chain with high rainfall gradients, varied habitats, high endemism and globally important freshwater and forest ecosystems.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Indian states that contain parts of the Western Ghats is correct?

options.A: The Western Ghats states from north to south include Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu
options.B: The Western Ghats states are only Karnataka and Kerala
options.C: The Western Ghats states are only Maharashtra and Goa
options.D: The Western Ghats states are only Tamil Nadu and Kerala

questions.explanation: The Western Ghats states from north to south include Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about examples of endemic fauna associated with the Western Ghats is correct?

options.A: Examples include lion-tailed macaque, Nilgiri tahr, Nilgiri langur and several endemic amphibians and freshwater fishes associated with the region; distributions differ by species
options.B: The only endemic fauna of the Western Ghats is the lion-tailed macaque
options.C: The only endemic fauna of the Western Ghats is the Nilgiri tahr
options.D: The only endemic fauna of the Western Ghats is the Nilgiri langur

questions.explanation: Examples include lion-tailed macaque, Nilgiri tahr, Nilgiri langur and several endemic amphibians and freshwater fishes associated with the region; distributions differ by species.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about examples of endemic or characteristic flora of the Western Ghats is correct?

options.A: The region supports many endemic plants, including species of Strobilanthes (kurinji) and numerous endemic trees, orchids and medicinal plants; exact endemism is species-specific
options.B: The only endemic plant of the Western Ghats is Strobilanthes
options.C: The only endemic plants of the Western Ghats are orchids
options.D: The only endemic plants of the Western Ghats are medicinal plants

questions.explanation: The region supports many endemic plants, including species of Strobilanthes (kurinji) and numerous endemic trees, orchids and medicinal plants; exact endemism is species-specific.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Nilgiri tahr is correct?

options.A: The Nilgiri tahr is an endangered mountain ungulate endemic to the southern Western Ghats, especially high-elevation grassland and rocky habitats
options.B: The Nilgiri tahr is an endangered primate
options.C: The Nilgiri tahr is a type of bird
options.D: The Nilgiri tahr is a type of freshwater fish

questions.explanation: The Nilgiri tahr is an endangered mountain ungulate endemic to the southern Western Ghats, especially high-elevation grassland and rocky habitats.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the lion-tailed macaque is correct?

options.A: The lion-tailed macaque is an endangered primate endemic to the Western Ghats, recognised by its black body and silver-white mane and tail tuft; it depends on tropical evergreen forests
options.B: The lion-tailed macaque is an endangered mountain ungulate
options.C: The lion-tailed macaque is a type of bird
options.D: The lion-tailed macaque is a type of freshwater fish

questions.explanation: The lion-tailed macaque is an endangered primate endemic to the Western Ghats, recognised by its black body and silver-white mane and tail tuft; it depends on tropical evergreen forests.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the importance of protected areas in Karnataka is correct?

options.A: Protected areas in Karnataka conserve Western Ghats forests, dry forests, wetlands and grasslands and provide habitat for elephants, tigers, gaur, endemic species and migratory birds
options.B: Protected areas in Karnataka only protect tigers
options.C: Protected areas in Karnataka only protect elephants
options.D: Protected areas in Karnataka have no biodiversity value

questions.explanation: Protected areas in Karnataka conserve Western Ghats forests, dry forests, wetlands and grasslands and provide habitat for elephants, tigers, gaur, endemic species and migratory birds.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about important national parks in Karnataka is correct?

options.A: Examples include Bandipur, Nagarahole (Rajiv Gandhi), Bannerghatta, Kudremukh, Anshi/Kali and parts of other protected landscapes; verify current official notifications for legal names and boundaries
options.B: The only national park in Karnataka is Bandipur
options.C: The only national park in Karnataka is Nagarahole
options.D: The only national park in Karnataka is Bannerghatta

questions.explanation: Examples include Bandipur, Nagarahole (Rajiv Gandhi), Bannerghatta, Kudremukh, Anshi/Kali and parts of other protected landscapes; verify current official notifications for legal names and boundaries.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the difference between a national park, sanctuary and biosphere reserve is correct?

options.A: A national park and sanctuary are statutory protected-area categories under Indian wildlife law; a biosphere reserve is a landscape-level designation under the UNESCO MAB framework and may include protected areas and inhabited sustainable-use zones
options.B: They are all the same
options.C: A biosphere reserve is a statutory category under Indian wildlife law
options.D: A national park is a UNESCO designation

questions.explanation: A national park and sanctuary are statutory protected-area categories under Indian wildlife law; a biosphere reserve is a landscape-level designation under the UNESCO MAB framework and may include protected areas and inhabited sustainable-use zones.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about a seed bank is correct?

options.A: A seed bank is a facility that stores seeds under controlled conditions to conserve plant genetic resources for future use, research and restoration
options.B: A seed bank is a facility that stores animal genetic material only
options.C: A seed bank is a type of national park
options.D: A seed bank is a type of botanical garden

questions.explanation: A seed bank is a facility that stores seeds under controlled conditions to conserve plant genetic resources for future use, research and restoration.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about captive breeding is correct?

options.A: Captive breeding is managed breeding of threatened animals outside or within protected settings to support conservation, genetic management and possible reintroduction
options.B: Captive breeding is breeding of crops only
options.C: Captive breeding is breeding of plants only
options.D: Captive breeding is a type of in-situ conservation

questions.explanation: Captive breeding is managed breeding of threatened animals outside or within protected settings to support conservation, genetic management and possible reintroduction.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about environmental pollution is correct?

options.A: Environmental pollution is an undesirable change in the physical, chemical or biological characteristics of air, water or land that harms organisms, ecosystems or human health
options.B: Environmental pollution is only air pollution
options.C: Environmental pollution is only water pollution
options.D: Environmental pollution is only soil pollution

questions.explanation: Environmental pollution is an undesirable change in the physical, chemical or biological characteristics of air, water or land that harms organisms, ecosystems or human health.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about air pollution is correct?

options.A: Air pollution is contamination of the atmosphere by harmful gases, particles or biological materials at concentrations that can affect health or the environment
options.B: Air pollution is only contamination by gases
options.C: Air pollution is only contamination by particles
options.D: Air pollution is contamination of water bodies

questions.explanation: Air pollution is contamination of the atmosphere by harmful gases, particles or biological materials at concentrations that can affect health or the environment.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about major air pollutants is correct?

options.A: Major air pollutants include particulate matter (PM2.5 and PM10), sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, carbon monoxide, ground-level ozone, volatile organic compounds, ammonia, lead and certain toxic air pollutants
options.B: The only major air pollutant is particulate matter
options.C: The only major air pollutant is carbon monoxide
options.D: The only major air pollutant is sulphur dioxide

questions.explanation: Major air pollutants include particulate matter (PM2.5 and PM10), sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, carbon monoxide, ground-level ozone, volatile organic compounds, ammonia, lead and certain toxic air pollutants.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about PM2.5 and PM10 is correct?

options.A: PM2.5 and PM10 are particulate matter with aerodynamic diameters of 2.5 micrometres or less and 10 micrometres or less, respectively; fine particles can penetrate deep into the lungs
options.B: PM2.5 and PM10 are gases with molecular weights of 2.5 and 10
options.C: PM2.5 and PM10 are types of ozone
options.D: PM2.5 and PM10 are types of nitrogen oxides

questions.explanation: PM2.5 and PM10 are particulate matter with aerodynamic diameters of 2.5 micrometres or less and 10 micrometres or less, respectively; fine particles can penetrate deep into the lungs.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about major sources of air pollution is correct?

options.A: Major sources of air pollution include vehicle exhaust, power plants, industries, construction and road dust, waste burning, household solid fuels, agricultural residue burning and natural sources such as dust storms and wildfires
options.B: The only source of air pollution is vehicle exhaust
options.C: The only source of air pollution is power plants
options.D: The only source of air pollution is natural sources

questions.explanation: Major sources of air pollution include vehicle exhaust, power plants, industries, construction and road dust, waste burning, household solid fuels, agricultural residue burning and natural sources such as dust storms and wildfires.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the effects of air pollution is correct?

options.A: Effects of air pollution include respiratory and cardiovascular disease, premature mortality, reduced visibility, crop damage, ecosystem acidification and climate effects depending on the pollutant
options.B: The only effect of air pollution is respiratory disease
options.C: The only effect of air pollution is reduced visibility
options.D: The only effect of air pollution is crop damage

questions.explanation: Effects of air pollution include respiratory and cardiovascular disease, premature mortality, reduced visibility, crop damage, ecosystem acidification and climate effects depending on the pollutant.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about water pollution is correct?

options.A: Water pollution is contamination or alteration of water quality that makes it harmful or unsuitable for drinking, aquatic life, agriculture or other uses
options.B: Water pollution is only contamination by sewage
options.C: Water pollution is only contamination by industrial chemicals
options.D: Water pollution is only contamination by plastics

questions.explanation: Water pollution is contamination or alteration of water quality that makes it harmful or unsuitable for drinking, aquatic life, agriculture or other uses.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about eutrophication is correct?

options.A: Eutrophication is excess nutrient enrichment of water, often by nitrogen and phosphorus, causing excessive algal or plant growth and sometimes oxygen depletion and fish kills
options.B: Eutrophication is depletion of nutrients in water
options.C: Eutrophication is increase in oxygen levels in water
options.D: Eutrophication is decrease in water temperature

questions.explanation: Eutrophication is excess nutrient enrichment of water, often by nitrogen and phosphorus, causing excessive algal or plant growth and sometimes oxygen depletion and fish kills.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about BOD is correct?

options.A: BOD is the amount of dissolved oxygen used by microorganisms to break down biodegradable organic matter in a water sample under specified test conditions; high BOD often indicates organic pollution
options.B: BOD is the amount of oxygen produced by photosynthesis
options.C: BOD is the amount of oxygen required for chemical oxidation only
options.D: BOD is the amount of oxygen in the atmosphere

questions.explanation: BOD is the amount of dissolved oxygen used by microorganisms to break down biodegradable organic matter in a water sample under specified test conditions; high BOD often indicates organic pollution.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about COD is correct?

options.A: COD is an analytical measure of the oxygen equivalent required to chemically oxidise substances in water; it is often used as an indicator of pollution load
options.B: COD is the amount of oxygen used by microorganisms
options.C: COD is the amount of oxygen produced by plants
options.D: COD is the amount of oxygen in the atmosphere

questions.explanation: COD is an analytical measure of the oxygen equivalent required to chemically oxidise substances in water; it is often used as an indicator of pollution load.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about soil pollution is correct?

options.A: Soil pollution is contamination of soil by harmful chemicals, salts, pathogens or wastes at levels that damage soil function, organisms, crops or human health
options.B: Soil pollution is only contamination by pesticides
options.C: Soil pollution is only contamination by industrial waste
options.D: Soil pollution is only contamination by plastics

questions.explanation: Soil pollution is contamination of soil by harmful chemicals, salts, pathogens or wastes at levels that damage soil function, organisms, crops or human health.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about common causes of soil pollution is correct?

options.A: Common causes of soil pollution include excessive pesticides and fertilisers, industrial waste, mining, oil spills, landfill leakage, sewage sludge contamination and improper disposal of hazardous waste
options.B: The only cause of soil pollution is excessive pesticides
options.C: The only cause of soil pollution is industrial waste
options.D: The only cause of soil pollution is mining

questions.explanation: Common causes of soil pollution include excessive pesticides and fertilisers, industrial waste, mining, oil spills, landfill leakage, sewage sludge contamination and improper disposal of hazardous waste.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about noise pollution is correct?

options.A: Noise pollution is unwanted or excessive sound that can harm health or interfere with normal activities and wildlife
options.B: Noise pollution is only loud music
options.C: Noise pollution is only industrial noise
options.D: Noise pollution is only traffic noise

questions.explanation: Noise pollution is unwanted or excessive sound that can harm health or interfere with normal activities and wildlife.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the effects of prolonged noise exposure is correct?

options.A: Effects of prolonged noise exposure include hearing loss, sleep disturbance, stress, impaired concentration and cardiovascular effects; wildlife communication and behaviour can also be disrupted
options.B: The only effect of prolonged noise exposure is hearing loss
options.C: The only effect of prolonged noise exposure is sleep disturbance
options.D: The only effect of prolonged noise exposure is stress

questions.explanation: Effects of prolonged noise exposure include hearing loss, sleep disturbance, stress, impaired concentration and cardiovascular effects; wildlife communication and behaviour can also be disrupted.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about thermal pollution is correct?

options.A: Thermal pollution is an undesirable change in the temperature of a natural water body, often from discharge of heated industrial or power-station cooling water, which can reduce dissolved oxygen and stress aquatic organisms
options.B: Thermal pollution is pollution caused by cold water
options.C: Thermal pollution is pollution caused by air
options.D: Thermal pollution is pollution caused by soil

questions.explanation: Thermal pollution is an undesirable change in the temperature of a natural water body, often from discharge of heated industrial or power-station cooling water, which can reduce dissolved oxygen and stress aquatic organisms.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about radioactive pollution is correct?

options.A: Radioactive pollution is the presence or release of radioactive substances or ionising radiation in the environment at levels that can cause harmful exposure
options.B: Radioactive pollution is pollution caused by sound
options.C: Radioactive pollution is pollution caused by heat
options.D: Radioactive pollution is pollution caused by light

questions.explanation: Radioactive pollution is the presence or release of radioactive substances or ionising radiation in the environment at levels that can cause harmful exposure.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about marine pollution is correct?

options.A: Marine pollution is the introduction of harmful substances or energy into seas and oceans, including plastics, oil, sewage, nutrients, chemicals, noise and heat
options.B: Marine pollution is only plastic pollution
options.C: Marine pollution is only oil pollution
options.D: Marine pollution is only sewage pollution

questions.explanation: Marine pollution is the introduction of harmful substances or energy into seas and oceans, including plastics, oil, sewage, nutrients, chemicals, noise and heat.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about plastic pollution is correct?

options.A: Plastic pollution is the accumulation of plastic materials in the environment, where they can injure wildlife, fragment into smaller particles and persist for long periods
options.B: Plastic pollution is only plastic in oceans
options.C: Plastic pollution is only plastic on land

questions.explanation: Plastic pollution is the accumulation of plastic materials in the environment, where they can injure wildlife, fragment into smaller particles and persist for long periods.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about microplastics is correct?

options.A: Microplastics are plastic particles generally smaller than 5 millimetres; they may be manufactured at small sizes or form when larger plastics fragment
options.B: Microplastics are plastic particles larger than 10 centimetres
options.C: Microplastics are only plastic particles found in the atmosphere
options.D: Microplastics are only plastic particles found in soil

questions.explanation: Microplastics are plastic particles generally smaller than 5 millimetres; they may be manufactured at small sizes or form when larger plastics fragment.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about industrial pollution is correct?

options.A: Industrial pollution arises from industrial processes, including emissions, wastewater, solid residues, hazardous chemicals, heat and noise
options.B: Industrial pollution is only air emissions from industries
options.C: Industrial pollution is only wastewater from industries
options.D: Industrial pollution is only solid waste from industries

questions.explanation: Industrial pollution arises from industrial processes, including emissions, wastewater, solid residues, hazardous chemicals, heat and noise.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about agricultural pollution is correct?

options.A: Agricultural pollution is environmental contamination from farming, including nutrient runoff, pesticides, soil erosion, livestock waste, salinity and agricultural plastic waste
options.B: Agricultural pollution is only pesticide pollution
options.C: Agricultural pollution is only nutrient runoff
options.D: Agricultural pollution is only livestock waste

questions.explanation: Agricultural pollution is environmental contamination from farming, including nutrient runoff, pesticides, soil erosion, livestock waste, salinity and agricultural plastic waste.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about domestic waste pollution is correct?

options.A: Domestic waste pollution is pollution from household sewage, detergents, food waste, plastics, oils, medicines and other discarded materials
options.B: Domestic waste pollution is only sewage pollution
options.C: Domestic waste pollution is only plastic pollution
options.D: Domestic waste pollution is only food waste pollution

questions.explanation: Domestic waste pollution is pollution from household sewage, detergents, food waste, plastics, oils, medicines and other discarded materials.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about pollution prevention is correct?

options.A: Pollution prevention is avoiding or reducing pollutants at their source through cleaner production, efficient resource use, safer substitutes, process control and good waste management
options.B: Pollution prevention is treating pollution after it is generated
options.C: Pollution prevention is diluting pollutants in the environment
options.D: Pollution prevention is moving pollutants to another location

questions.explanation: Pollution prevention is avoiding or reducing pollutants at their source through cleaner production, efficient resource use, safer substitutes, process control and good waste management.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about wastewater treatment is correct?

options.A: Wastewater treatment involves physical, biological and chemical processes used to remove solids, organic matter, nutrients, pathogens and other contaminants from wastewater
options.B: Wastewater treatment involves only physical processes
options.C: Wastewater treatment involves only biological processes
options.D: Wastewater treatment involves only chemical processes

questions.explanation: Wastewater treatment involves physical, biological and chemical processes used to remove solids, organic matter, nutrients, pathogens and other contaminants from wastewater.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the usual stages of sewage treatment is correct?

options.A: The usual stages are preliminary treatment (screens and grit removal), primary settling, secondary biological treatment and, where needed, tertiary/advanced treatment and disinfection
options.B: The usual stages are only primary and secondary treatment
options.C: The usual stages are only tertiary treatment
options.D: The usual stages are only disinfection

questions.explanation: The usual stages of sewage treatment are preliminary treatment (screens and grit removal), primary settling, secondary biological treatment and, where needed, tertiary/advanced treatment and disinfection.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about primary sewage treatment is correct?

options.A: During primary sewage treatment, physical processes such as screening and sedimentation remove large solids, grit and settleable suspended matter
options.B: During primary sewage treatment, microorganisms break down organic matter
options.C: During primary sewage treatment, nutrients are removed
options.D: During primary sewage treatment, pathogens are disinfected

questions.explanation: During primary sewage treatment, physical processes such as screening and sedimentation remove large solids, grit and settleable suspended matter.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about secondary sewage treatment is correct?

options.A: During secondary sewage treatment, microorganisms biologically break down dissolved and suspended biodegradable organic matter, commonly in activated-sludge or biofilm systems
options.B: During secondary sewage treatment, large solids are removed by screening
options.C: During secondary sewage treatment, nutrients are removed by chemical precipitation
options.D: During secondary sewage treatment, pathogens are removed by disinfection

questions.explanation: During secondary sewage treatment, microorganisms biologically break down dissolved and suspended biodegradable organic matter, commonly in activated-sludge or biofilm systems.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about tertiary sewage treatment is correct?

options.A: Tertiary sewage treatment is additional treatment to remove nutrients, remaining suspended solids, dissolved contaminants or pathogens, depending on the intended discharge or reuse
options.B: Tertiary sewage treatment is primary settling
options.C: Tertiary sewage treatment is screening and grit removal
options.D: Tertiary sewage treatment is secondary biological treatment

questions.explanation: Tertiary sewage treatment is additional treatment to remove nutrients, remaining suspended solids, dissolved contaminants or pathogens, depending on the intended discharge or reuse.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about solid waste management is correct?

options.A: Solid waste management is the systematic segregation, collection, storage, transport, processing, recovery and safe disposal of solid waste
options.B: Solid waste management is only collection and disposal
options.C: Solid waste management is only segregation
options.D: Solid waste management is only recycling

questions.explanation: Solid waste management is the systematic segregation, collection, storage, transport, processing, recovery and safe disposal of solid waste.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about biomedical waste is correct?

options.A: Biomedical waste is waste generated during diagnosis, treatment or immunisation of humans or animals, or in related research and biological production/testing, requiring regulated segregation and treatment
options.B: Biomedical waste is only waste from hospitals
options.C: Biomedical waste is only waste from laboratories
options.D: Biomedical waste is only waste from pharmacies

questions.explanation: Biomedical waste is waste generated during diagnosis, treatment or immunisation of humans or animals, or in related research and biological production/testing, requiring regulated segregation and treatment.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about e-waste is correct?

options.A: E-waste is discarded electrical and electronic equipment and its components; it may contain valuable materials as well as hazardous substances
options.B: E-waste is only discarded computers
options.C: E-waste is only discarded mobile phones

questions.explanation: E-waste is discarded electrical and electronic equipment and its components; it may contain valuable materials as well as hazardous substances.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about hazardous waste is correct?

options.A: Hazardous waste has properties such as toxicity, corrosivity, ignitability or reactivity that can pose substantial risks to health or the environment and requires special handling
options.B: Hazardous waste is only toxic waste
options.C: Hazardous waste is only corrosive waste
options.D: Hazardous waste is only ignitable waste

questions.explanation: Hazardous waste has properties such as toxicity, corrosivity, ignitability or reactivity that can pose substantial risks to health or the environment and requires special handling.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about plastic waste management is correct?

options.A: Plastic waste management includes prevention, segregation, collection, reuse, recycling, processing and environmentally sound disposal of discarded plastic, supported by producer responsibility and design improvements
options.B: Plastic waste management is only recycling
options.C: Plastic waste management is only disposal
options.D: Plastic waste management is only prevention

questions.explanation: Plastic waste management includes prevention, segregation, collection, reuse, recycling, processing and environmentally sound disposal of discarded plastic, supported by producer responsibility and design improvements.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about source segregation of waste is correct?

options.A: Source segregation of waste is separating waste where it is generated into appropriate streams, such as wet/biodegradable, dry/recyclable and domestic hazardous or sanitary waste, according to local rules
options.B: Source segregation of waste is separating waste at the landfill
options.C: Source segregation of waste is burning waste at the source
options.D: Source segregation of waste is transporting waste to another location

questions.explanation: Source segregation of waste is separating waste where it is generated into appropriate streams, such as wet/biodegradable, dry/recyclable and domestic hazardous or sanitary waste, according to local rules.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the 3R principle in waste management is correct?

options.A: The 3R principle means Reduce, Reuse and Recycle; reducing consumption and waste is generally the first priority
options.B: The 3R principle means Remove, Replace and Restore
options.C: The 3R principle means Reduce, Remove and Rebuild
options.D: The 3R principle means Reuse, Restore and Recycle

questions.explanation: The 3R principle means Reduce, Reuse and Recycle; reducing consumption and waste is generally the first priority.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about composting is correct?

options.A: Composting is the controlled biological decomposition of organic waste into a stable, soil-like material that can improve soil structure and nutrient content
options.B: Composting is burning of organic waste
options.C: Composting is landfilling of organic waste

questions.explanation: Composting is the controlled biological decomposition of organic waste into a stable, soil-like material that can improve soil structure and nutrient content.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about biodegradable waste is correct?

options.A: Biodegradable waste is waste that microorganisms can break down into simpler substances under suitable conditions, such as food scraps, leaves and many paper products
options.B: Biodegradable waste is waste that cannot be broken down by microorganisms
options.C: Biodegradable waste is only plastic waste
options.D: Biodegradable waste is only electronic waste

questions.explanation: Biodegradable waste is waste that microorganisms can break down into simpler substances under suitable conditions, such as food scraps, leaves and many paper products.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the harmlessness of biodegradable waste is correct?

options.A: No. Poorly managed biodegradable waste can generate methane, leachate, odours and pathogens; management conditions matter
options.B: Yes, it is always harmless

questions.explanation: No. Poorly managed biodegradable waste can generate methane, leachate, odours and pathogens; management conditions matter.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the waste hierarchy is correct?

options.A: The waste hierarchy is a preferred order of waste management: prevention/reduction, preparing for reuse, recycling, recovery and, as a last resort, disposal
options.B: The waste hierarchy is a list of waste types
options.C: The waste hierarchy is a method of waste burning
options.D: The waste hierarchy is a type of landfill

questions.explanation: The waste hierarchy is a preferred order of waste management: prevention/reduction, preparing for reuse, recycling, recovery and, as a last resort, disposal.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about leachate is correct?

options.A: Leachate is liquid that has percolated through waste and carries dissolved or suspended contaminants; it must be collected and treated at engineered landfills
options.B: Leachate is a type of gas from landfills
options.C: Leachate is a type of compost
options.D: Leachate is a type of plastic

questions.explanation: Leachate is liquid that has percolated through waste and carries dissolved or suspended contaminants; it must be collected and treated at engineered landfills.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about a sanitary landfill is correct?

options.A: A sanitary landfill is an engineered facility where waste is placed, compacted and covered with systems for leachate and gas management and environmental monitoring
options.B: A sanitary landfill is an open dumping ground
options.C: A sanitary landfill is a composting facility
options.D: A sanitary landfill is an incineration plant

questions.explanation: A sanitary landfill is an engineered facility where waste is placed, compacted and covered with systems for leachate and gas management and environmental monitoring.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the atmosphere is correct?

options.A: The atmosphere is the layer of gases surrounding Earth, held by gravity and essential for climate, weather and life
options.B: The atmosphere is only the ozone layer
options.C: The atmosphere is only the troposphere
options.D: The atmosphere is only the stratosphere

questions.explanation: The atmosphere is the layer of gases surrounding Earth, held by gravity and essential for climate, weather and life.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the approximate composition of dry air near Earth's surface is correct?

options.A: Dry air near Earth's surface is about 78.08% nitrogen, 20.95% oxygen, 0.93% argon and about 0.04% carbon dioxide, with trace gases; water vapour varies
options.B: Dry air is about 50% nitrogen and 50% oxygen
options.C: Dry air is about 20% nitrogen and 80% oxygen
options.D: Dry air is about 90% carbon dioxide and 10% oxygen

questions.explanation: Dry air near Earth's surface is about 78.08% nitrogen, 20.95% oxygen, 0.93% argon and about 0.04% carbon dioxide, with trace gases; water vapour varies.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the main layers of the atmosphere is correct?

options.A: The main layers of the atmosphere are troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, thermosphere and exosphere, based mainly on temperature structure
options.B: The main layers are troposphere, stratosphere and mesosphere only
options.C: The main layers are troposphere and stratosphere only
options.D: The main layers are mesosphere, thermosphere and exosphere only

questions.explanation: The main layers of the atmosphere are troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, thermosphere and exosphere, based mainly on temperature structure.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the layer where the ozone layer is concentrated is correct?

options.A: The ozone layer is concentrated in the stratosphere, mainly around 15-35 km altitude, though ozone is distributed over a wider range
options.B: The ozone layer is concentrated in the troposphere
options.C: The ozone layer is concentrated in the mesosphere
options.D: The ozone layer is concentrated in the thermosphere

questions.explanation: The ozone layer is concentrated in the stratosphere, mainly around 15-35 km altitude, though ozone is distributed over a wider range.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about weather is correct?

options.A: Weather is the short-term state of the atmosphere at a particular place and time, including temperature, rainfall, wind, humidity and cloud cover
options.B: Weather is the long-term statistical pattern of weather in a region

questions.explanation: Weather is the short-term state of the atmosphere at a particular place and time, including temperature, rainfall, wind, humidity and cloud cover.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about climate is correct?

options.A: Climate is the long-term statistical pattern of weather in a region, commonly assessed over periods of about 30 years or more
options.B: Climate is the short-term state of the atmosphere

questions.explanation: Climate is the long-term statistical pattern of weather in a region, commonly assessed over periods of about 30 years or more.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the greenhouse effect is correct?

options.A: The greenhouse effect is the warming of Earth's surface and lower atmosphere because greenhouse gases absorb and re-emit infrared radiation emitted by Earth
options.B: The greenhouse effect is the cooling of Earth's surface due to greenhouse gases
options.C: The greenhouse effect is the depletion of the ozone layer
options.D: The greenhouse effect is the formation of acid rain

questions.explanation: The greenhouse effect is the warming of Earth's surface and lower atmosphere because greenhouse gases absorb and re-emit infrared radiation emitted by Earth.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the major greenhouse gases is correct?

options.A: Major greenhouse gases include water vapour, carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide, ozone and fluorinated gases such as hydrofluorocarbons, perfluorocarbons, sulphur hexafluoride and nitrogen trifluoride
options.B: The only major greenhouse gas is carbon dioxide
options.C: The only major greenhouse gas is methane
options.D: The only major greenhouse gas is water vapour

questions.explanation: Major greenhouse gases include water vapour, carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide, ozone and fluorinated gases such as hydrofluorocarbons, perfluorocarbons, sulphur hexafluoride and nitrogen trifluoride.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the natural greenhouse effect is correct?

options.A: Yes, the natural greenhouse effect keeps Earth much warmer than it would otherwise be; human emissions are strengthening it and causing additional warming
options.B: No, the natural greenhouse effect is harmful
options.C: No, the natural greenhouse effect has no effect on temperature
options.D: Yes, but it only affects plants

questions.explanation: Yes. The natural greenhouse effect keeps Earth much warmer than it would otherwise be; human emissions are strengthening it and causing additional warming.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about global warming is correct?

options.A: Global warming is the long-term increase in Earth's average surface temperature, primarily driven in the modern era by human-caused greenhouse-gas emissions
options.B: Global warming is a short-term increase in temperature
options.C: Global warming is the cooling of Earth's surface
options.D: Global warming is the depletion of the ozone layer

questions.explanation: Global warming is the long-term increase in Earth's average surface temperature, primarily driven in the modern era by human-caused greenhouse-gas emissions.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about climate change is correct?

options.A: Climate change refers to long-term changes in climate patterns, including temperature, precipitation, sea level and extremes, caused by natural factors and human activities; recent global warming is predominantly human-caused
options.B: Climate change refers only to changes in temperature
options.C: Climate change refers only to changes in rainfall
options.D: Climate change refers only to changes in sea level

questions.explanation: Climate change refers to long-term changes in climate patterns, including temperature, precipitation, sea level and extremes, caused by natural factors and human activities; recent global warming is predominantly human-caused.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about a carbon footprint is correct?

options.A: A carbon footprint is the total greenhouse-gas emissions associated with an individual, product, organisation, activity or event, usually expressed as carbon dioxide equivalent (CO2e)
options.B: A carbon footprint is the physical footprint of a carbon atom
options.C: A carbon footprint is the amount of carbon in soil
options.D: A carbon footprint is the amount of carbon in the atmosphere

questions.explanation: A carbon footprint is the total greenhouse-gas emissions associated with an individual, product, organisation, activity or event, usually expressed as carbon dioxide equivalent (CO2e).

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the carbon cycle is correct?

options.A: The carbon cycle is the movement of carbon among the atmosphere, oceans, living organisms, soils, rocks and fossil fuels through processes such as photosynthesis, respiration, decomposition, ocean exchange and combustion
options.B: The carbon cycle is the movement of carbon only in the atmosphere
options.C: The carbon cycle is the movement of carbon only in the oceans
options.D: The carbon cycle is the movement of carbon only in living organisms

questions.explanation: The carbon cycle is the movement of carbon among the atmosphere, oceans, living organisms, soils, rocks and fossil fuels through processes such as photosynthesis, respiration, decomposition, ocean exchange and combustion.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about carbon sequestration is correct?

options.A: Carbon sequestration is the capture and long-term storage of carbon dioxide or carbon in vegetation, soils, oceans, geological formations or engineered systems
options.B: Carbon sequestration is the release of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere
options.C: Carbon sequestration is the burning of fossil fuels
options.D: Carbon sequestration is the formation of acid rain

questions.explanation: Carbon sequestration is the capture and long-term storage of carbon dioxide or carbon in vegetation, soils, oceans, geological formations or engineered systems.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the ozone layer is correct?

options.A: The ozone layer is a region of the stratosphere with relatively high ozone concentration that absorbs most harmful solar ultraviolet-B and ultraviolet-C radiation
options.B: The ozone layer is a region of the troposphere with high ozone concentration
options.C: The ozone layer is a region of the mesosphere
options.D: The ozone layer is a region of the thermosphere

questions.explanation: The ozone layer is a region of the stratosphere with relatively high ozone concentration that absorbs most harmful solar ultraviolet-B and ultraviolet-C radiation.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the causes of ozone-layer depletion is correct?

options.A: Ozone-depleting substances such as CFCs and halons release chlorine or bromine in the stratosphere, catalytically destroying ozone
options.B: Carbon dioxide emissions cause ozone-layer depletion
options.D: Sulphur dioxide emissions cause ozone-layer depletion

questions.explanation: Ozone-depleting substances such as CFCs and halons release chlorine or bromine in the stratosphere, catalytically destroying ozone.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the effects of ozone depletion is correct?

options.A: Effects of ozone depletion include more harmful UV-B reaching Earth's surface, increasing risks of skin cancer, cataracts and immune effects and harming crops, phytoplankton and ecosystems
options.B: The only effect of ozone depletion is skin cancer
options.C: The only effect of ozone depletion is cataracts
options.D: The only effect of ozone depletion is harm to crops

questions.explanation: Effects of ozone depletion include more harmful UV-B reaching Earth's surface, increasing risks of skin cancer, cataracts and immune effects and harming crops, phytoplankton and ecosystems.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about acid rain is correct?

options.A: Acid rain is precipitation or deposition made more acidic mainly by sulphuric and nitric acids formed from sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides in the atmosphere
options.B: Acid rain is rain made acidic by carbon dioxide only
options.C: Acid rain is rain made acidic by methane
options.D: Acid rain is rain made acidic by ozone

questions.explanation: Acid rain is precipitation or deposition made more acidic mainly by sulphuric and nitric acids formed from sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides in the atmosphere.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the major effects of acid rain is correct?

options.A: Major effects of acid rain include acidification of lakes and soils, damage to forests and aquatic life, nutrient leaching, mobilisation of toxic aluminium and corrosion of buildings and monuments
options.B: The only effect of acid rain is acidification of lakes
options.C: The only effect of acid rain is damage to forests
options.D: The only effect of acid rain is corrosion of buildings

questions.explanation: Major effects of acid rain include acidification of lakes and soils, damage to forests and aquatic life, nutrient leaching, mobilisation of toxic aluminium and corrosion of buildings and monuments.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about photochemical smog is correct?

options.A: Photochemical smog is air pollution formed when sunlight drives reactions involving nitrogen oxides and volatile organic compounds, producing ground-level ozone and other oxidants
options.B: Photochemical smog is smoke from burning coal
options.C: Photochemical smog is fog mixed with smoke
options.D: Photochemical smog is air pollution from sulphur dioxide only

questions.explanation: Photochemical smog is air pollution formed when sunlight drives reactions involving nitrogen oxides and volatile organic compounds, producing ground-level ozone and other oxidants.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about El Niño is correct?

options.A: El Niño is the warm phase of the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO), involving unusually warm sea-surface temperatures in the central/eastern equatorial Pacific and changes in atmospheric circulation
options.B: El Niño is the cool phase of ENSO
options.C: El Niño is a type of cyclone
options.D: El Niño is a type of monsoon

questions.explanation: El Niño is the warm phase of the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO), involving unusually warm sea-surface temperatures in the central/eastern equatorial Pacific and changes in atmospheric circulation.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about La Niña is correct?

options.A: La Niña is the cool phase of ENSO, involving unusually cool sea-surface temperatures in the central/eastern equatorial Pacific and associated atmospheric circulation changes
options.B: La Niña is the warm phase of ENSO
options.C: La Niña is a type of cyclone
options.D: La Niña is a type of monsoon

questions.explanation: La Niña is the cool phase of ENSO, involving unusually cool sea-surface temperatures in the central/eastern equatorial Pacific and associated atmospheric circulation changes.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about how El Niño can affect the Indian monsoon is correct?

options.A: El Niño is statistically associated with an increased likelihood of weaker Indian summer monsoon rainfall in many years, but the relationship is not deterministic and other climate drivers also matter
options.B: El Niño guarantees drought every year
options.C: El Niño has no effect on the Indian monsoon
options.D: El Niño guarantees excess rainfall every year

questions.explanation: El Niño is statistically associated with an increased likelihood of weaker Indian summer monsoon rainfall in many years, but the relationship is not deterministic and other climate drivers also matter.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Indian monsoon is correct?

options.A: The Indian monsoon is a seasonal reversal of winds associated with land-sea heating contrasts and large-scale atmospheric-oceanic circulation, bringing most of India's annual rainfall during the southwest monsoon season
options.B: The Indian monsoon is a type of cyclone
options.C: The Indian monsoon is a type of drought
options.D: The Indian monsoon is a type of flood

questions.explanation: The Indian monsoon is a seasonal reversal of winds associated with land-sea heating contrasts and large-scale atmospheric-oceanic circulation, bringing most of India's annual rainfall during the southwest monsoon season.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about extreme weather events is correct?

options.A: Extreme weather events are events such as heat waves, intense rainfall, droughts, floods and severe storms that are unusual or hazardous relative to local climate conditions
options.B: Extreme weather events are only heat waves
options.C: Extreme weather events are only floods
options.D: Extreme weather events are only droughts

questions.explanation: Extreme weather events are events such as heat waves, intense rainfall, droughts, floods and severe storms that are unusual or hazardous relative to local climate conditions.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about a drought is correct?

options.A: A drought is a prolonged period of abnormally low water availability relative to normal conditions, affecting rainfall, soil moisture, rivers, reservoirs or groundwater
options.B: A drought is a short period of heavy rainfall
options.C: A drought is a type of cyclone
options.D: A drought is a type of flood

questions.explanation: A drought is a prolonged period of abnormally low water availability relative to normal conditions, affecting rainfall, soil moisture, rivers, reservoirs or groundwater.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about a flood is correct?

options.A: A flood is overflow or accumulation of water on land that is normally dry, caused by intense rainfall, river overflow, storm surge, dam failure or other factors
options.B: A flood is a prolonged period of low rainfall
options.C: A flood is a type of cyclone
options.D: A flood is a type of drought

questions.explanation: A flood is overflow or accumulation of water on land that is normally dry, caused by intense rainfall, river overflow, storm surge, dam failure or other factors.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about a tropical cyclone is correct?

options.A: A tropical cyclone is a rotating, organised low-pressure storm system that forms over warm tropical or subtropical waters and has strong winds and heavy rainfall
options.B: A tropical cyclone is a type of drought
options.C: A tropical cyclone is a type of flood
options.D: A tropical cyclone is a type of heat wave

questions.explanation: A tropical cyclone is a rotating, organised low-pressure storm system that forms over warm tropical or subtropical waters and has strong winds and heavy rainfall.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about a heat wave is correct?

options.A: A heat wave is a period of unusually hot weather relative to local conditions, often lasting several days and posing risks to health, agriculture and infrastructure; operational thresholds vary by region
options.B: A heat wave is a period of unusually cold weather
options.C: A heat wave is a type of cyclone
options.D: A heat wave is a type of flood

questions.explanation: A heat wave is a period of unusually hot weather relative to local conditions, often lasting several days and posing risks to health, agriculture and infrastructure; operational thresholds vary by region.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about desertification is correct?

options.A: Desertification is land degradation in arid, semi-arid and dry sub-humid areas resulting from climatic variations and human activities; it is not simply the spread of existing deserts
options.B: Desertification is the spread of existing deserts only
options.C: Desertification is the formation of new deserts only
options.D: Desertification is a type of drought

questions.explanation: Desertification is land degradation in arid, semi-arid and dry sub-humid areas resulting from climatic variations and human activities; it is not simply the spread of existing deserts.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the causes of sea-level rise is correct?

options.A: Sea-level rise is primarily caused by thermal expansion of warming seawater and addition of water from melting glaciers and ice sheets; local land movement also affects relative sea level
options.B: Sea-level rise is only caused by melting glaciers
options.C: Sea-level rise is only caused by thermal expansion of seawater
options.D: Sea-level rise is only caused by local land movement

questions.explanation: Sea-level rise is primarily caused by thermal expansion of warming seawater and addition of water from melting glaciers and ice sheets; local land movement also affects relative sea level.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about glacier retreat is correct?

options.A: Glacier retreat is the reduction in a glacier's mass and extent when ice loss exceeds accumulation over time, commonly associated with a warming climate
options.B: Glacier retreat is the growth of a glacier
options.C: Glacier retreat is the formation of a new glacier
options.D: Glacier retreat is the movement of a glacier

questions.explanation: Glacier retreat is the reduction in a glacier's mass and extent when ice loss exceeds accumulation over time, commonly associated with a warming climate.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about climate adaptation is correct?

options.A: Climate adaptation is adjusting human or natural systems to actual or expected climate impacts to reduce harm or take advantage of beneficial opportunities
options.B: Climate adaptation is reducing greenhouse-gas emissions
options.C: Climate adaptation is increasing greenhouse-gas emissions
options.D: Climate adaptation is ignoring climate impacts

questions.explanation: Climate adaptation is adjusting human or natural systems to actual or expected climate impacts to reduce harm or take advantage of beneficial opportunities.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about climate mitigation is correct?

options.A: Climate mitigation is reducing greenhouse-gas emissions or increasing greenhouse-gas removals, for example through clean energy, energy efficiency, forest protection and carbon capture
options.B: Climate mitigation is adjusting to climate impacts
options.C: Climate mitigation is ignoring climate change
options.D: Climate mitigation is increasing greenhouse-gas emissions

questions.explanation: Climate mitigation is reducing greenhouse-gas emissions or increasing greenhouse-gas removals, for example through clean energy, energy efficiency, forest protection and carbon capture.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about sustainable development is correct?

options.A: Sustainable development is development that meets present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs, integrating economic, social and environmental dimensions
options.B: Sustainable development is development that ignores environmental concerns
options.C: Sustainable development is development that only focuses on economic growth
options.D: Sustainable development is development that only focuses on environmental protection

questions.explanation: Sustainable development is development that meets present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs, integrating economic, social and environmental dimensions.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Paris Agreement is correct?

options.A: The Paris Agreement is a legally binding international treaty adopted in 2015 under the UNFCCC, aiming to hold global temperature rise well below 2°C and pursue efforts to limit it to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels
options.B: The Paris Agreement is a treaty to phase out ozone-depleting substances
options.C: The Paris Agreement is a treaty on biological diversity
options.D: The Paris Agreement is a treaty on wetlands

questions.explanation: The Paris Agreement is a legally binding international treaty adopted in 2015 under the UNFCCC, aiming to hold global temperature rise well below 2°C and pursue efforts to limit it to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) is correct?

options.A: NDCs are climate action plans submitted by Parties to the Paris Agreement, describing their mitigation and, where relevant, adaptation commitments; they are updated in successive cycles
options.B: NDCs are a list of ozone-depleting substances
options.C: NDCs are a list of biodiversity hotspots
options.D: NDCs are a list of wetlands

questions.explanation: NDCs are climate action plans submitted by Parties to the Paris Agreement, describing their mitigation and, where relevant, adaptation commitments; they are updated in successive cycles.

questions.subject: Environmental Science & Ecology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Kyoto Protocol is correct?

options.A: The Kyoto Protocol was a 1997 protocol to the UNFCCC that established legally binding greenhouse-gas emission reduction targets for many developed countries for commitment periods
options.B: The Kyoto Protocol was a 1987 treaty to phase out ozone-depleting substances
options.C: The Kyoto Protocol was a 1992 treaty on biological diversity
options.D: The Kyoto Protocol was a 1971 treaty on wetlands

questions.explanation: The Kyoto Protocol was a 1997 protocol to the UNFCCC that established legally binding greenhouse-gas emission reduction targets for many developed countries for commitment periods.
